title: Trying something new
scene: An indoor rock-climbing wall in a sports hall. A girl in a white helmet and a harness is high up on the wall, reaching for the next hold and looking up. Below her, a boy holds her safety rope with one hand and points up to show her where to go. A taller boy beside him is pointing too, and other students stand close by, looking up and calling out to her.
imagePrompt: A realistic wide photograph inside a Singapore secondary school sports hall with a tall indoor rock-climbing wall. A sixteen-year-old Singaporean Chinese girl in a white helmet, a climbing harness and a plain blue T-shirt is high up on the wall, three metres above the floor, reaching for the next hold with a slightly nervous expression, a safety rope running up from her harness. On the floor below, a sixteen-year-old Malay boy holds the other end of her rope with both hands, looking up. Beside him three Singaporean teenagers aged sixteen in plain sports T-shirts and shorts look up and cheer with raised arms. A male instructor points up at a hold. Bright indoor light, candid documentary style, no text, no logos.
planned: Would you like to try an activity like this? Why or why not?
interaction: Why are some people afraid to try new things?
Should schools make every student take part in outdoor activities? Why or why not?
Is it more important to win or to take part? Explain your view.
